title: FancyZones exclude by pressing shift during drag no longer working

status.label: Stable regression reproduced; fix is in Preview
status.detail: Merged PR #49985 fixes the mid-drag Shift state and a commenter verified it in Preview; Stable v0.101.2362 predates that fix.

judgment.rationale: The original report isolates a mid-drag Shift transition with “hold Shift to enable zones” disabled. The commenter explains the hook ordering and identifies merged PR #49985 as the fix, reporting the behavior corrected in v0.101.2781 Preview. Current Stable v0.101.2362 predates that fix, so the issue should not be considered fixed for Stable until a stable build includes it.
evidence: On v0.101.2362.0, Shift held before dragging excludes the window, but pressing it during the drag still snaps it.
The latest user comment says PR #49985 fixed the swallowed-Shift state and verifies the behavior on v0.101.2781 Preview.
Merged PR #49985 records Shift state before the hook swallows the key and adds tests.
Current Stable is v0.101.2362.0; current Preview is v0.102.2911.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify current Stable and Preview; keep tracked until the merged fix ships in Stable, then close with the fix link.

fix_assessment.rationale: Merged PR #49985 contains the mid-drag Shift fix and tests; the commenter reports it working in Preview. Stable release coverage still needs a maintainer check.

issue_context.summary: With Shift-to-enable disabled, pressing Shift mid-drag should exclude the window, but 0.101.2362 Stable still snaps; the merged fix is reported working in Preview.
known_information: Issue build: v0.101.2362.0; sequence uses Notepad.
Shift before drag works; pressing it during the same drag fails.
Reporter supplied Windows 11 build 26200.9106, German Windows, system installation.
A commenter explains the hook swallowed Shift before WM_INPUT and says PR #49985 sets drag state before returning.
The commenter reports success on v0.101.2781 Preview.
PR #49985 is merged; current Stable v0.101.2362 predates the reported fixed Preview.
inferences: The regression is fixed in code represented by PR #49985, but Stable may remain affected until a stable release contains it.
issue_context.analysis: The report and latest comment align with the merged code/test fix. Since the target is Stable and confirmation is on Preview, closure should wait for stable shipment rather than be inferred from merge alone.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and both comments, including the user’s 2026-10-07 confirmation.
Verified PR #49985 is merged and describes the same swallowed-Shift defect and tests.
Checked live releases: Stable is v0.101.2362.0 and Preview is v0.102.2911.0.

actions.label: Verify Shift fix in Stable and Preview

reproduce.version_requirement: Compare current Stable v0.101.2362.0 with current Preview v0.102.2911.0
prerequisites: Enable FancyZones and configure a visible zone layout.
Turn off “Hold Shift key to activate zones while dragging.”
Use a Notepad window and a known zone.
steps: On Stable, drag Notepad without Shift, press and hold Shift during the drag, then release the mouse while Shift remains held.
Confirm whether it snaps; repeat with Shift held before drag as a control.
Review app-zone history or applied zone state, not only the transient overlay.
reproduce.expected_result: Stable may reproduce until the fix ships; Preview should not snap on a mid-drag Shift transition.
setup_requirements: Record the exact build and whether zones remain active after pressing Shift.

judgment.rationale: The report is a complete current-version regression scenario. Current source has a DraggingState Shift latch and UI tests that explicitly expect mid-drag Shift to hide zones, so the next step is to reproduce the release behavior against that state machine and fix the event-order gap.
evidence: Notepad reproduces on 0.101.2362 after update; Shift held before drag works, Shift pressed during drag does not.
Current FancyZones UI tests specify that, with shiftDrag=false, pressing Shift during a drag deactivates zones.
DraggingState receives Shift through raw input and derives snapping from Shift XOR secondary-mouse state.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the existing mid-drag Shift test against the release-equivalent build and fix whichever raw-input/drop transition leaves snapping active.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged fix was found for this mid-drag regression; current code and tests identify a narrow state-ordering boundary.

proposed_fixes.title: Apply mid-drag Shift state before the final snap decision
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The live 0.101 build appears to reach MoveSizeEnd with stale snapping state when Shift changes after drag start, despite the intended raw-input state transition and regression-test expectation.
plan: Reproduce using the exact shiftDrag=false sequence and capture DraggingState::SetShiftState, UpdateDraggingState, and MoveSizeEnd ordering.
Ensure a Shift make received during an active drag updates snapping/overlay state before the mouse-up snap decision.
Strengthen DragWindowTests so the assertion verifies the final app-zone history after pressing Shift mid-drag, not only visual state.
verification: Run FancyZones DragWindowTests for shiftDrag=false and mid-drag Shift.
Verify Shift before drag and Shift during drag both exclude the window, while no Shift still snaps.
Repeat with non-primary mouse switching enabled and disabled.

confidence.rationale: The intended state machine and regression test are present, but a release-build reproduction is needed to locate whether input delivery, state update, or final drop ordering fails.

upstream_safety.detail: No upstream or fork issue/PR writes were made.
